queries_attempted: incident response timeline automatic logging post-mortem

competitors.name: Incident.io
competitors.notes: Purpose-built for Slack-native incident management. Automatically creates incident channels, declares incidents with /incident command, captures timeline of events, assigns roles, and integrates with PagerDuty/Statuspage. Auto-generates post-incident reviews. This is the closest direct competitor - they solve exactly this JTBD.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automatic event/timestamp logging, Slack integration, PagerDuty integration, role assignment tracking, post-incident review generation, timeline export
competitors.pricing: Free for up to 5 users; Pro starts at $16/user/month; Enterprise with custom pricing
competitors.market_positioning: Slack-first incident management platform; 'Incidents made easy in Slack'

competitors.name: FireHydrant
competitors.notes: Full incident management platform with automated runbooks, auto-generated incident timelines, and post-mortem templates. Integrates with Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog. Automatically tracks who did what and when, generates retrospective documents. Direct competitor.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automatic event logging, timestamp tracking, PagerDuty integration, Slack integration, post-mortem generation, role tracking, runbook automation
competitors.pricing: Free tier available; Teams at $500/month; Enterprise custom pricing
competitors.market_positioning: Reliability platform for incident response; focuses on full lifecycle from alert to retrospective

competitors.name: Blameless
competitors.notes: SRE platform with automated incident timelines, post-mortem workflows, and reliability insights. Captures all actions during an incident, generates structured post-mortems. Direct competitor targeting SRE teams explicitly.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automated timeline, post-mortem generation, Slack/PagerDuty integration, action tracking, retrospective analysis
competitors.market_positioning: SRE platform for reliability engineering; 'From incident response to blameless postmortems'

competitors.name: Rootly
competitors.notes: Incident management built on Slack. Automates incident processes, creates auto-generated timelines, tracks actions and timestamps, generates post-mortems. Very close competitor also Slack-native.
competitors.feature_overlap: Slack-native incident management, auto-timeline, post-mortem generation, PagerDuty integration, action logging
competitors.pricing: Starts at $4,000/year for 50 users; scales with organization size
competitors.market_positioning: Slack-native incident management; 'Manage incidents directly from Slack'

competitors.name: Jeli (acquired by PagerDuty)
competitors.notes: Incident analysis platform acquired by PagerDuty. Focuses on incident learning and analysis. Can ingest data from various sources to build incident narratives. Now part of PagerDuty's offering, making it a platform-native threat.
competitors.feature_overlap: Incident data aggregation, narrative building, analysis for post-mortems, PagerDuty integration
competitors.pricing: Part of PagerDuty Enterprise plans; not sold standalone
competitors.market_positioning: Incident analysis from PagerDuty; learning-focused rather than response-focused

competitors.name: PagerDuty Process Automation (formerly Rundeck)
competitors.notes: PagerDuty's own platform has expanded with Process Automation and analytics. With the Jeli acquisition, they're building out post-incident capabilities. Platform-native threat - existing PagerDuty users get incident timelines and can add post-mortem features.
competitors.feature_overlap: Incident timeline (through Jeli), alert logging, action automation, limited post-mortem capabilities
competitors.pricing: Business plans start at $41/user/month; Enterprise custom pricing
competitors.market_positioning: Full digital operations platform; incident management as part of broader offering

competitors.name: OpsGenie (Atlassian)
competitors.notes: Alerting and incident management from Atlassian. Has incident timelines, alert logging, and integration with Confluence for post-mortems. Partial competitor - has the pieces but requires more manual assembly of the post-mortem workflow.
competitors.feature_overlap: Alert aggregation, incident timeline, Slack integration, basic post-mortem templates via Confluence integration
competitors.pricing: Starting at $19/user/month for professional; integrated with Atlassian suite
competitors.market_positioning: Critical incident management as part of Atlassian DevOps stack

competitors.name: Grafana Incident
competitors.notes: Incident management built into Grafana. Automates incident declaration, documents timeline, and creates post-incident review docs. For teams already using Grafana, this is an easy add-on. Partial competitor as it's more tied to observability workflows.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automated timeline, Slack integration, post-incident review document, role assignment
competitors.pricing: Included in Grafana Cloud Advanced ($299/month) or can be purchased separately
competitors.market_positioning: Incident management for observability teams; tightly integrated with Grafana ecosystem

competitors.name: Squadcast
competitors.notes: SRE incident management platform with automated incident timelines, post-mortem features, and action tracking. Specifically designed for SRE teams. Direct competitor with a strong focus on the SRE user persona.
competitors.feature_overlap: Auto incident timeline, post-mortem templates, Slack/PagerDuty integration, automated action logging, SLO tracking
competitors.pricing: Starts at $18/user/month for Premium; Enterprise at $39/user/month
competitors.market_positioning: SRE-focused incident management; 'Built by SREs for SREs'

competitors.name: Zebrium (acquired by ScienceLogic)
competitors.notes: AI-driven incident root cause analysis. Uses machine learning to automatically correlate logs and events, finding root cause without manual detective work. Different approach (AI correlation vs. manual timeline logging) but solves the outcome of producing accurate post-mortems faster.
competitors.feature_overlap: Automated event correlation, incident timeline generation, root cause identification
competitors.market_positioning: AI incident root cause analysis; substitute approach using ML

competitors.name: Incident Post-Mortem Templates (various open source)
competitors.notes: Collection of post-mortem templates from companies like Google, Atlassian, and PagerDuty. Not software, but provides templates that engineers can use with manual timeline data. Low-friction alternative for documentation-focused teams.
competitors.feature_overlap: Post-mortem structure and guidance only; no automation
competitors.market_positioning: Open-source templates and guidance for incident reviews

competitors.name: Morgue (Etsy open source)
competitors.notes: Open-source post-mortem tool from Etsy. Provides structured post-mortem creation with categories, timelines, and action items. Requires manual data entry but provides structure for the post-mortem process.
competitors.feature_overlap: Post-mortem structure, timeline documentation (manual), action item tracking
competitors.market_positioning: Open-source post-mortem documentation tool from Etsy; lightweight

substitutes.description: ServiceNow Incident Management module with post-incident review capabilities
substitutes.notes: Large enterprises often use ServiceNow for ITSM which includes incident management and post-incident review. Enterprise-grade but heavy and expensive.

substitutes.description: Manual Google Docs/wiki post-mortem process with templates
substitutes.notes: Many organizations use structured post-mortem templates in Google Docs, Confluence, or Notion with engineers manually compiling data. This is the most common 'competitor' in practice.

substitutes.description: Consulting firms offering incident management process optimization
substitutes.notes: Several consultancies (e.g., Adaptive SRE, Verica) offer incident management consulting and process improvement, which can reduce need for purpose-built software.

summary: This is a crowded, well-established market with multiple well-funded, purpose-built direct competitors. The category includes at least 6-7 named direct competitors (incident.io, FireHydrant, Blameless, Rootly, Squadcast, Grafana Incident, PagerDuty/Jeli) and several strong partial competitors from platform companies (Atlassian/OpsGenie, PagerDuty, Grafana). Several of these companies have raised significant venture capital (FireHydrant $31.5M, incident.io $28.7M, Blameless $20M+). The Slack-native angle is well-covered by multiple players (incident.io, Rootly). The SRE-specific angle is directly addressed by Squadcast, Blameless, and FireHydrant. Open-source alternatives exist but are mostly templates. The competitive moat would need to be significant to compete - perhaps automated root cause correlation (like Zebrium) or AI-generated post-mortems (differentiation). The market is heating up with consolidation (PagerDuty acquiring Jeli, ServiceNow acquiring various tools). This is a Score 4 ('crowded market with established alternatives') bordering on Score 5 given the maturity and funding of competitors.
